name: Purpleish
lede: Purpleish is a dusty, reddish purple: a crowd name from the 2010 xkcd color survey, where people typed in whatever word fit the swatch they were shown.

sections.title: A survey word, not a coined one
sections.body:
The name comes from the xkcd color survey of 2010, where respondents typed free-text names for colors on screen, and this was one of the results kept [1]. No book or earlier dictionary in our sources records it; its origin is undocumented beyond that survey [1]. It is simply [[purple]] plus the suffix "-ish", softening the claim rather than naming a new hue [1].

The nearest named color on file is [[razzmic-berry]], 3.3 units away and almost the same shade [2]. [[mathews-purple]] sits at 3.7, lighter and a touch bluer, and [[antique-fuchsia]] further off, redder [2]. The survey's "Purplish", spelled without the extra *e*, landed only 0.9 units away, closer than any of those [2]. Our library files both spellings under Razzmic Berry [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color within six units of this one, over at least five percent of the canvas, in a single painting: Georges Dupuis's *Notre-Dame Embankment, Le Havre* of 1908, as photographed [3]. One painting is too thin a record to say anything about how the color behaves in paint; the survey measured word choice, not pigment [3].
